subject: Announcement: community occupancy models with camtrapR

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Announcement: community occupancy models with camtrapR
parts:
Dear all, 
the R package camtrapR can now create community occupancy models automatically with a new function called "communityModel". It:
  • automatically writes model code for community occupancy models in JAGS or Nimble
  • sets inits and selects parameters to monitor
  • allows fixed and random effects
  • bundles all relevant input data into a convenient object (for which several methods exist)
  • calculates various derived quantities (e.g. residuals, Bayesian p-values, species richness)
  • allows for optional data augmentation (fully open community or known maximum species richness)
In addition there are methods for:
  • fitting models,
  • plotting model estimates,
  • plotting marginal effects,
  • creating predictions of occupancy probabilities and species richness (including spatial predictions)
The function is intended to be general and not restricted to camera trapping data. 

It is included in the the GitHub version of camtrapR which can be installed via:
install_github("jniedballa/camtrapR", build_vignettes = TRUE)
 
See vignette 5 in the package for more details and examples: (based on data simulated with the AHMbook package)
vignette("camtrapr5", package = "camtrapR")

The function code is here: 
https://github.com/jniedballa/camtrapR/blob/master/R/communityModel.R

Please feel free to reach out if you should have any questions. It is a first release, so things may change a little in the future. Also, there are still some limitations which will be addressed in the future, e.g. allowing customizable priors.
 
Best regards,
 
Jürgen

parts:
Minor addition: Installation from GitHub with build_vignettes = TRUE requires the package R.rsp due to the static vignettes.
Hence, first:

if(!"R.rsp" %in% installed.packages()) install.packages("R.rsp")

then 
library(remotes)
